skills.name: Change in mass when carbonates are heated

note.text:
When a carbonate is heated in an open crucible, carbon dioxide escapes, so the mass of the solid decreases.
Method: weigh the empty crucible; add the carbonate and weigh again; heat strongly; cool and weigh; heat, cool and weigh again until the mass stops changing (constant mass).
Mass of carbon dioxide lost = mass before heating − mass after heating.
Percentage loss = mass lost ÷ mass of carbonate × 100.
For calcium carbonate: 100 g gives 56 g of calcium oxide and 44 g of carbon dioxide, so the loss is always 44%.
The total mass is conserved: the missing mass is the gas that escaped.

worked_example.problem: {a} g of calcium carbonate is heated to constant mass. {b} g of solid remains. Find the mass lost and the percentage loss.

cards.idea: Heating a carbonate in an open crucible makes it lighter: carbon dioxide escapes.
example: The solid left is the oxide.

cards.idea: Mass lost = mass before − mass after.

check.prompt: A carbonate of mass {a} g is heated to constant mass. {b} g of solid remains. What mass of carbon dioxide was lost?

misconceptions.explain: Subtract: the gas that escaped is the difference.

cards.idea: Heat to constant mass to make sure all the carbonate has decomposed.

check.prompt: {a} g of calcium carbonate loses {l} g on heating. What is the percentage loss?

misconceptions.explain: That is the mass; divide by the starting mass and × {100}.

pick.q: Why does the mass of calcium carbonate decrease when heated in an open crucible?
w: Oxygen from the air is added.

pick.q: Why do we heat to constant mass?
pick.r: to make sure all the carbonate has decomposed
pick.y: When the mass stops changing, the reaction is complete.
